name: Geomagnetic-rotation probe (Wang 2019 trial structure)
origin: Trial structure after Wang et al. 2019 (Caltech: Kirschvink, Shimojo; University of Tokyo: Matani); the ring version is a project construct
summary: Six runs of about 7 min, each with 162 pseudorandom trials 2-3 s apart: in a sweep trial the field travels once around the eight-coil ring in 100 ms (12.5 ms per coil), in a fixed trial it stays on the front coil (Fpz) for 100 ms. It copies the trial structure of the only published uT-scale human EEG magnetoreception study (Wang 2019) and is meant for EEG: alpha (8-13 Hz) desynchronisation after sweep versus fixed trials.
notes: Wang et al. 2019 used three-axis coils to rotate a uniform field of about 35 uT (the ambient magnitude) around a participant in a dark Faraday chamber, in 100-ms rotations of the field direction (the 9.1 uT horizontal component turned by 90 degrees; the largest stimulus was a 150-degree arc) against fixed trials, and reported an alpha-power drop after one rotation type only (downward-directed, counter-clockwise). This helmet can only move a local field around the ring, about 6-12 times weaker, and cannot rotate the geomagnetic vector, whose static vertical component mattered in Wang's result. In a sweep the field glides from Fpz once around the ring and back (360 degrees; the coils are blended by the engine's linear crossfade instead of the research's cosine crossfade); sweep and fixed trials have the same length and strength, so they differ only in movement. A phase can play only two tracks, so direction is not randomised per trial: runs 1, 3 and 5 sweep counter-clockwise seen from above (Fpz, F7, T7 ...), runs 2, 4 and 6 clockwise. Each run repeats its own 135-s pseudorandom block (27 sweep, 27 fixed, at most 3 of a kind in a row) three times; trial onsets are the table's full-scale points (100 ms each) counted from the start of the run, which an EEG analysis needs as markers. Fades are off so every trial has full strength; the 1-min rests are a project choice. Left out: the optional DC background on the start coil between trials and Wang's double-wrapped sham coils; check for induced EEG artefacts by running the program on a saline phantom, and use the app's Blind option for sham runs (its sham switches the current off, so unlike Wang's antiparallel windings it does not reproduce current-related artefacts). Without the background, a fixed trial is a 100-ms pulse on Fpz rather than Wang's no-change trial. A real replication needs a three-axis coil system around the whole head (about 100 uT range, with ambient-field control). Single-lab result with no independent replication found; expect a null result.
setting: Seated, eyes closed, in total darkness and quiet, with EEG (alpha 8-13 Hz, analysed after sweep versus fixed trials). Wang's participants sat in a dark, shielded chamber; sessions took about 1 h.
schedule: One session per sitting; no repetition schedule was part of the original study.
source: Wang et al. 2019, eNeuro, Transduction of the geomagnetic field as evidenced from alpha-band activity in the human brain https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6494972/
